name: Kernel Integrity Check
description: Checks kernel compilation signatures in /proc/version and uname, bootloader lock state from /proc/cmdline, and kptr_restrict address visibility in /proc/kallsyms, and cross-checks the kernel release the process inherited from Zygote against the live uname() release and its procfs exports.

evidenceUnits.title: Kernel and boot integrity posture
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Kernel build strings, version signatures, bootloader parameters, and kallsyms address visibility
evidenceUnits.proposition: An available kernel or boot observation matches a maintained integrity-posture rule
evidenceUnits.availability: Each observation depends on kernel configuration, procfs permissions, and platform exposure
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The running kernel owns all returned sources and can conceal or rewrite them
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A marker or visibility state is bounded evidence and does not prove a malicious custom kernel

evidenceUnits.title: Kernel release identity across sources
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The kernel release string as recorded in the os.version system property inherited from Zygote, returned by a live uname() call, and exported by /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease and /proc/version
evidenceUnits.proposition: Two readable sources report different kernel releases, which an unmodified device cannot do because the release cannot change while the kernel runs
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: System.getProperty("os.version") through JNI, the uname() syscall, and bounded procfs reads
evidenceUnits.availability: Comparable when at least two sources are readable; the Zygote snapshot and uname() normally are, while an app's SELinux domain usually cannot read the procfs exports
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Crosses from the release Zygote recorded before this app started to what the kernel returns now; a kernel hook can rewrite each live source, and an in-process hook can rewrite the Java property
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A disagreement shows that some source was rewritten, not which one or by which tool; agreement is a concealable negative, because a spoof applied before Zygote initialises makes every source carry the same spoofed release
